news.Title: Amazon stock pops after Morgan Stanley details 5 catalysts, lifts price target
news.Content: Amazon ( AMZN ) stock rose more than 3% in early trading on Monday after Morgan Stanley named it a top pick and raised its price target to $350 from $335, outlining five catalysts that could drive the stock higher. The new target implies about 40% upside from Friday's close of $250. With a bear case of $220 a share and a bull case of $410, the firm sees a 3:1 risk-reward ratio. "In a market of see-sawing AI leaders and laggards, we detail 5 catalysts ahead to re-rate shares and drive material outperformance," analyst Brian Nowak, who kept his Overweight rating, wrote in a note Sunday. 5 catalysts for Amazon Faster AWS growth: Morgan Stanley now expects revenue at AWS, Amazon's cloud unit, to grow 47% in 2027 and 42% in 2028, up from 41% and 37%. The change follows Nvidia's ( NVDA ) disclosure that it expects AWS to buy and deploy about 2 million of its GPUs over those two years. The extra chips also lift the firm's capital spending forecast for Amazon to $355 billion in 2027 and $365 billion in 2028. Bigger AWS profits: Nowak expects AWS operating margins of 42% in 2027 and 44% in 2028, which supports about $16.50 in Amazon earnings per share in 2028. Bedrock: More visibility into Bedrock, Amazon's AI model service, could lift the stock's valuation from about 15 times 2028 earnings, according to the note. AI shopping: Nowak expects Amazon to emerge as a winner as AI shopping agents spread and expects it to partner over time with Meta's ( META ) Muse AI agent . The holiday season is the first big test. Robotics: Every 10% of Amazon's global units that move through its robotics-enabled fulfillment centers could save $2 billion to $4 billion a year, Morgan Stanley estimates. The firm calls robotics a 2027 catalyst. Amazon stock is up about 11% this year but sits roughly 10% below its early August high. Earlier this month, Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi noted that Amazon was trading at one of its lowest trailing price-to-earnings ratios in years . Morgan Stanley's $350 target is based on about 21 times its 2028 earnings estimate. Amazon reports third quarter results on Oct. 29 after the bell. news.Title: Stock market today: Dow slips, Nasdaq, S&P 500 rise as the AI trade rebounds
news.Content: US stocks were mixed on Monday, led by a rebound in the technology ( XLK ) sector as investors looked ahead to earnings from Tesla ( TSLA ) and Meta ( META ) this week. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) rose 1% while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) gained 0.5%. Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 0.2% after all three major averages ended the week lower on Friday. The Nasdaq is coming off its worst weekly performance since June, while the S&P 500 is rising after a nearly 2% drop last week. Semiconductor stocks edged higher, led by shares of Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD ( AMD ). Shares of Nvidia-backed CoreWeave ( CRWV ) gained on the heels of a Buy upgrade from Goldman Sachs. Shares of the neocloud provider sank 25% last week amid AI financing worries. Tesla will report earnings on Wednesday after the EV maker unveiled a jaw-dropping redesign of the Roadster last week. Social Media giant Meta will also post results on the same day. Streaming giant Netflix ( NFLX ) will report after the close on Tuesday. Oil prices were steady with Brent crude ( BZ=F ) at $108 per barrel after Ukraine struck oil facilities in Russia and tankers came under attack in the Middle East. West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) dropped to $98. LIVE 6 updates 6 mins ago Jared Blikre 'Black Monday' turns 39 Thirty-nine years ago today, the Dow ( DOW ) plunged 508 points. That was nearly 23% of its value, gone before the closing bell. Mike Zaccardi marks the anniversary on X with the next morning's New York Times front page. Beneath the enormous crash headline, a smaller one asked: "Does 1987 Equal 1929?" For a little perspective, a Black Monday -sized drop from Friday's Dow close near 52k would erase roughly 11,750 points . In this log-scale chart of the S&P 500 on AlphaSpace, you can see the steep drop not far from the left edge. That would get your attention — and generate some big headlines. Some of the trouble came from portfolio insurance , a strategy meant to protect investors by selling stock-index futures as prices fell. More selling pushed prices lower, triggering still more selling. The protection was new at the time and helped feed the panic. It's not unheard of in financial "innovation" to run amock . The crash helped usher in circuit breakers , giving markets a timeout when selling gets extreme. The Fed stepped in the next morning before the open, and the Dow recovered 57% of Black Monday's point loss over the next two sessions. The crash also prompted President Ronald Reagan to create the President's Working Group on Financial Markets in March 1988—later nicknamed the "Plunge Protection Team," or PPT. 33 mins ago David Hollerith US stocks open mixed as Friday's tech selloff reverses US stocks rose slightly at Monday's open as chipmakers are leading tech stocks higher, reversing last week's selloff. The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 ( ^IXIC ) rose 1.1% while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) gained 0.5% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) was little changed after all three major averages ended the week lower on Friday. Investors are turning attention to earnings from some of the market's biggest giants this week including Tesla ( TSLA ) and Meta ( META ), as Wall Street looks for evidence that strong profit growth can revive enthusiasm around the artificial intelligence trade. 48 mins ago Jared Blikre Tech is leading again as October's winning trades reverse Chips are leading tech stocks ( XLK ) higher after last week's beating. Energy ( XLE ) and consumer staples ( XLP ) have gone from October's best-performing sectors to Monday's worst. The iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) rose 3.6% in premarket trading, recovering part of last week's roughly 12% decline. Micron ( MU ), AMD ( AMD ) and Intel were among the chipmakers bouncing back. Those stocks helped power the spring advance as US-Iran ceasefire hopes improved. Last week, many of those earlier winners took the biggest hits as investors questioned the cost of financing the AI buildout. Monday's early moves are reversing that rotation. The decline of prior winners this morning extends beyond energy and staples. Among October's 100 strongest performers in the S&P 500 through Friday, roughly 91% of those showing a premarket change are lower. Meanwhile, 77% of October's worst performers are heading higher. Spring's leaders are returning, while the stocks that offered shelter during the recent selling are giving up ground. For SOXX, reclaiming and holding roughly $515 would recover Friday's decline — the first hurdle after last week's beating. Today at 1:05 PM UTC David Hollerith Saylor's Strategy rebounds after $193 million preferred stock buyback Shares of Strategy ( MSTR ), bitcoin's biggest corporate holder, rose early Monday after the firm, led by bitcoin influencer Michael Saylor, disclosed that it repurchased $193 million of its Stretch ( STRC ) preferred shares last week along with $22 million buying bitcoin. The disclosure comes after Strategy's common stock fell nearly 10% on Friday , its worst single-day in nearly eight months. The company said that it also increased its authorized stock buyback from $2 billion to $3 billion. Strategy also added 267 bitcoins, bringing its total bitcoin stash to 848,517. Last Thursday, index provider MSCI announced new eligibility rules that could lead to Strategy's removal from its global stock indexes, potentially forcing index-tracking funds to sell its shares. MSCI said it will publish its final list of affected companies on Nov. 11. Strategy reports third quarter earnings later this month. Today at 12:30 PM UTC Ines Ferré Homebuyers are canceling sales at near-record rates Yahoo Finance's Claire Boston reports: Homebuyers are backing out of contracts at near-record rates, a potential sign of how higher mortgage rates are prompting buyers to rethink their plans. Nationwide, 14.5% of homes fell out of contract in September, according to Redfin data, the highest share on record apart from the early months of the COVID-19 pandemic. Homes can fall out of contract for a number of reasons, such as inspection findings or financing pitfalls, or when a buyer just has a change of heart. But pending sales tend to fall through at higher rates when buyers have more options and more negotiating power, as they currently do in much of the country. Today at 11:44 AM UTC Ines Ferré BofA economists maintains likelihood of Fed rate hike this month BofA economists still see an October rate hike on the table, despite most of the market pricing in an unchanged policy decision for next week, and an increase in December. The economists point out that the inflation picture has gotten worse since the September meeting. However, 85% of market participants expect policymakers to keep rates steady when they meet next week. "Most of the FOMC was on board with two hikes this year. Why not do the second one in Oct, to retain the optionality for a third in Dec?" wrote BofA economist Aditya Bhave on Monday. "We have low conviction as to whether he is serious about bringing a "sea change" to the Fed. But we're giving him the benefit of the doubt, by retaining our Oct hike forecast," added Bhave. news.Title: Microsoft pulls out of UK Nscale data centre deal over power delay
news.Content:
By Paul Sandle

LONDON, Oct 19 (Reuters) - Microsoft has pulled out of a deal to anchor a flagship data centre for Nvidia-backed Nscale after power connection delays pushed ‌its expected supply date into the 2030s, highlighting a major obstacle to Britain's ‌AI ambitions.

The US tech giant said on Monday it remained committed to its partnership with Nscale, including work to ​build digital infrastructure and support AI growth globally.

"This decision relates to a single site," a Microsoft spokesperson said of its termination of an agreement for the data centre in Loughton, Essex, where Nscale had faced delays, with electricity grid officials telling the AI company they did not expect to ‌supply power to the site until ⁠the 2030s.

"Our relationship with Microsoft remains strong and long-term, and this unfortunate London-wide grid issue has no impact on our other contracts," a spokesperson ⁠for Nscale told Reuters.

"We remain committed to both the Loughton project and the UK, and we are exploring alternative power sources for the site, as well as other expansion sites in the UK," they ​added.

Microsoft's ​move was first reported by the Telegraph newspaper.

The project ​was among technology deals announced during ‌US President Donald Trump's visit in September 2025 and intended to showcase Britain's ambition to become a global AI leader.

But that faces a major constraint in the form of electricity supply, with bottlenecks in grid connection queues delaying data centre projects by as long as 13 years.

The Loughton site was due to begin operating early next year, with 23,040 Nvidia GB300 GPUs providing ‌50 megawatts of AI computing capacity to help power ​Microsoft's Azure services in Britain, the companies said last ​year.

Nscale filed for an initial public ​offering in the United States last month, with Microsoft and Anthropic expected to ‌be among its major customers, according to ​its prospectus.

The group provides ​infrastructure, including computing capacity, power and data centres, as well as software for training and running AI models.

Nscale has grown rapidly since launch, increasing its total contracted value ​from $100 million to more than $103 ‌billion in two-and-a-half years. It competes with AI infrastructure providers CoreWeave, Nebius, Crusoe and ​Lambda.

(Reporting by Nethra Sailesh and Gnaneshwar Rajan in Bengaluru and Paul Sandle in ​London; Editing by Joe Bavier and Alexander Smith)

news.Title: Google’s Next AI Chip Is Running Late. Why Marvell May Be Fine
news.Content:
Google's next TPU chip is reportedly facing delays. Still, GF Securities believes Marvell Technology Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL ) remains well-positioned in Google's chip supply chain over the medium and long term. How should investors interpret the delay for Marvell's stock? If you're weighing MRVL's AI growth potential against short-term uncertainty, these 11 AI stocks are worth a closer look, with Marvell securing the No. 7 spot.

A Delay, Not a Demand Problem

GF Securities says one part of Google's TPU v9 design has slipped by about three weeks, likely due to a redesign. That small delay pushes the timeline back by about a quarter. Tape-out is now scheduled for January 2027, mass production for the second quarter of 2027, and shipments for the first quarter of 2028. Packaging substrate yields are a key obstacle, at just 45% to 50%. However, GF Securities believes it has identified the underlying causes of the problem.

The firm does not see demand as a concern. GF analyst Jeff Pu highlights strong demand for Google's TPUs from both Google itself and external customers, including Anthropic. GF suggests that this external demand may be one reason Gemini 4 is arriving later than expected, as a significant share of Google's TPU v7 went to outside customers in the first half of 2026. The firm identifies MediaTek, rather than Marvell, as facing short-term headwinds. Because the note offers no specific details about Marvell's role in the supply chain, any benefit from the situation appears indirect. However, Jeff Pu's own posts associate v9 with MediaTek, whereas Marvell's potential Google opportunity involves later-generation chips and remains uncertain. As a result, the delay is unlikely to have much direct impact on Marvell. The delay may not change MRVL's short-term outlook, but its AI potential keeps it on investors' radar. Explore our list of 10 AI stocks that could skyrocket, featuring Marvell .

Does Google's Delay Move Marvell's Stock?

At 63x forward earnings, Marvell trades at a 66% premium to its five-year average P/E of 38.02x. So the stock does not look undervalued. Using estimates for the next fiscal year, the multiple comes down to approximately 37x to 40x, near the average, although the two measures use different bases. Investors are paying up for strong earnings growth. EPS is projected to increase 48.59% this fiscal year and 72.58% the next year, with growth accelerating rather than easing.

But that valuation leaves little room for delays. Investors are paying upfront for growth that must arrive on schedule. At its recent investor day, management set long-term targets of roughly $80 billion in revenue and $30 in non-GAAP EPS by calendar year 2030, according to Morningstar. The current premium reflects expectations for that growth. However, Marvell does not seem to generate meaningful revenue from TPU v9, which GF's analyst attributes to MediaTek. As a result, the delay has only a limited, indirect impact on the stock and is not, by itself, a reason to buy.

Story Continues

In my view, the premium is justified only if Marvell delivers the expected growth on time. If that still doesn't impress you, you can compare it with 9 other stocks in our list of Top 10 Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) Stocks to Buy in 2026 .

Hedge fund ownership of Marvell grew from 79 funds at the end of Q1 2026 to 96 at the end of Q2 2026. Short interest accounted for 3.21% of float as of September 30, 2026.

GF's comments indicate that Marvell's longer-term position in Google's chip supply chain remains intact. But the note does not specify Marvell's role, while rising hedge fund ownership signals broader institutional participation. Still, a 63x multiple on this year's earnings leaves little room for delays. The company needs to deliver on the expected timeline to support its valuation.

While we acknowledge the potential of MRVL as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT ) has long been treated as the safer way to own cloud computing, supported by its corporate subscriptions, large customers, and an established profit stream. Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) is beginning to complicate that argument.

Yet Yahoo Finance's latest valuation data shows that Microsoft is trading at 25.13 times forward earnings against 22.83 times for Alphabet. Its 30% operating-income growth is the more defensible figure for evaluating underlying performance.

Yahoo Finance's most recently available valuation snapshots put Microsoft at 25.13 times forward earnings and Amazon at 23.64 times.

That narrow gap begs investor attention because Microsoft's enterprise software produces enormous profits alongside Azure, while Amazon is using profits from AWS and its retail operations to fund an infrastructure buildout that has pushed free cash flow below zero.

The question investors need to look into is not which cloud provider is growing faster. It is how much of that growth remains available to shareholders after the computers, data centers, and supporting infrastructure have been paid for. news.Title: Meta vs. Alphabet: Is GOOGL’s AI Growth Being Overlooked by Investors?
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META ) and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) have become two of the biggest investors in artificial intelligence, but their latest results pose an uncomfortable question: how much of that spending is already producing returns?

Both giants are growing advertising revenue, and yet their cash flows tell a less straightforward story, which is significant for investors because their valuations are remarkably close. Yahoo Finance's latest available valuation data places Meta at 22.08 times forward earnings and Alphabet at 22.83 times.

The numbers show that investors are assigning roughly the same earnings multiple to two companies making very different bets on AI infrastructure. Let's take a deeper look at this. But before that, we meticulously compiled a list of the best big name stocks to buy according to financial media, and there are eight stocks other than GOOGL and META that rank on that list. Access the complete list for free here.

Bull Case

Meta's advertising business is performing better than its profit figures initially suggest. Second-quarter revenue increased 28% to $60.8 billion, with ad impressions rising 14% year-over-year and average price per ad climbing 12% year-over-year. Those figures suggest growth came from both advertising volume and pricing, and not merely a larger audience. Daily users across its apps increased a much more modest 3% to 3.60 billion. The contrast points to stronger monetization of the audience Meta already has.

In other news, an ex-Google researcher said AI could "Kill Us All". Should Alphabet investors care? Meanwhile, Alphabet has a second profit engine that distinguishes it from Meta. Google Cloud revenue rose 82% to $24.8 billion. This is especially relevant to the valuation because Alphabet's growing cloud business is contributing material earnings and not just remaining an expensive undertaking whose commercial success is still hypothetical.

Google's established advertising operation has also continued to grow. Google Search and other revenue increased to $63.3 billion from $54.2 billion a year earlier. Alphabet further reported that its total operating income rose 30% to $40.8 billion, faster than its 24% revenue growth. Quarterly spending rose 55% year-over-year to $42.0 billion, although that includes $2.4 billion in legal charges and $1.18 billion of severance costs in connection with its May 2026 headcount reduction. These items help explain why operating income declined 8% despite strong revenue growth, but they also make it misleading to treat the entire expense increase as recurring AI investment.

Story Continues

Still, its infrastructure commitments are substantial. Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META ) spent $31.08 billion on capital expenditures, including finance-lease principal payments, leaving just $784 million of free cash flow despite $31.86 billion in operating cash inflows. Meta also recently made a substantial C$13 billion bet in Alberta to bolster its infrastructure advantage. But would it be able to do so? Read our article for insight. Management also expects full-year capital expenditures of $130 billion to $145 billion. The advertising engine is generating cash, but much of it is being redirected into infrastructure.

Alphabet presents a different accounting trap. Its reported EPS jumped to $9.11, but a net gain on equity securities added approximately $6.26 per share after tax. That investment gain should not be confused with recurring growth from Search or Cloud.

Alphabet's free cash flow was also negative $5.86 billion in the quarter. Even with Cloud delivering strong profits, the company invested more in physical infrastructure than its operating cash flow generated that quarter, and so its capital intensity is no longer a footnote to the AI story.

Conclusion

Similar forward P/E ratios conceal different economics when it comes to these two giants. Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META ) is improving advertising monetization while making a heavy investment whose future returns remain unproven. Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) has already turned rapid cloud growth into significant operating income, but its infrastructure spending is consuming substantial cash too.

The more useful valuation question is not which company mentions AI more often, but how much additional operating profit and free cash flow those investments can generate without requiring spending to keep rising at the same pace.

news.Title: Meta Tested Broadcom’s CPO for 1 Million Port-Hours. What It Found
news.Content:
On October 13, Micas Networks announced three new switches built on Broadcom's Tomahawk 6 chip. One of them is a compact co-packaged optics (CPO) switch using Broadcom's Tomahawk 6-Davisson, with production expected in early 2027. I believe that matters because Broadcom's CPO has mostly been used by large cloud companies so far. A switch from an independent vendor could give other data centers a way to adopt the technology too. It also highlights how long Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO ) has been at this.

Davisson is its third generation of CPO switches, following its first in 2021. It can move 102.4 terabits of data per second, which Broadcom says was double any other CPO switch available when it launched in October 2025. Broadcom's latest CPO switch highlights its role in next-generation data centers but its only 4th on our list of Top 10 Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) Stocks to Buy in 2026 .

Why Broadcom's Headstart Matters

Being early only counts if the technology works, and Broadcom has the proof. In a paper presented in October 2025, Meta tested Broadcom's previous-generation CPO switches for one million cumulative device hours without a single link failure. It also found they used 65% less power per lane than traditional pluggable optics (about 35% less than linear-drive optics). Reliability has been the main worry holding CPO back, so that kind of data is hard for rivals to match. Davisson hasn't published equivalent data yet, and Broadcom isn't alone: Nvidia's Spectrum-X Photonics CPO switch is now in full production, with CoreWeave, Lambda, and Oracle among its early adopters. Still, I think Broadcom's years of field data give it a strong position when customers are ready to make the switch. The company's years of CPO development could pay off as adoption expands. But which other stocks Reddit users think could take off ?

Growth Makes the Premium Look Reasonable

Broadcom trades above its historical average, and the premium makes sense to me. The forward non-GAAP P/E of 30.43x is about 11% above its 5-year average, while the forward Price-to-sales ratio of 15.98x is 22% higher. The EPS outlook helps justify the multiples. Analysts expect earnings to rise about 71% this fiscal year and 66% the next. That would bring the P/E down to roughly 18x on fiscal 2027 earnings. CPO is still a small part of Broadcom's business today, and much of that growth comes from its custom AI chips. Still, CPO gives Broadcom another way to grow as AI networks get bigger. Broadcom carries about $35 billion in net debt, which seems manageable for a $1.69 trillion company.

Story Continues

Hedge fund ownership held fairly steady as funds holding Broadcom slipped from 173 in Q1 to 170 in Q2. The value of their stakes fell from $32.8 billion to $29.1 billion.

Broadcom has spent years proving CPO works. As the technology spreads beyond the largest cloud companies, I think its head start could help it win a meaningful share of that new demand.

news.Content:
According to Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: LITE ) CEO Michael Hurlston, the company is now almost sold out of components for 2029, as he said in a recent interview. Just six months ago, he said Lumentum was on track to sell out by 2028. The demand outlook is strong, but Lumentum's strong demand raises the question of how much growth is already priced in. Meanwhile, see our Top 10 Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) Stocks to Buy in 2026 to see the 5 companies that rank higher than LITE.

Demand Isn't the Problem

The underlying details paint a more limited picture. Lumentum cannot meet about 70% of demand for certain products through next year. For some other products, supply constraints will leave 30% of demand unmet through 2028.

According to Wedbush Securities' Matt Bryson, this creates a favorable backdrop for optical-input suppliers such as AXT and for foundry and silicon photonics companies, including Tower Semiconductor and GlobalFoundries. The challenge is not a lack of demand but limited capacity. LITE's growth will depend on how quickly it can expand production. Lumentum's challenge is turning strong demand into actual sales, but which other aggressive growth stocks do Wall Street analysts see as having room to run ?

Is a 46x Multiple Fair?

Lumentum's forward P/E stands at 45.70x, roughly 22% above its five-year average of 37.51x. This indicates that investors are paying more than they have historically. That premium reflects expectations for rapid earnings growth. EPS is projected to grow 151.24% this fiscal year from a small base, followed by another 64.80% increase next year. Based on current estimates, the P/E could decline to roughly 28x on 2028 earnings and 21x on 2029 earnings. This means much of the earnings investors are paying for today is expected to arrive within one to three years. The company's near sold-out capacity lends more support to those projections.

The stock is not undervalued, but its premium could be reasonable if Lumentum adds capacity as planned. Demand is already there; production capacity is now the key factor limiting growth.

According to our database, the number of hedge funds holding Lumentum fell from 123 at the end of Q1 2026 to 111 at the end of Q2 2026. Short interest reached 8.96% of float as of September 30, 2026.

While demand remains firm and Wedbush sees potential benefits for Lumentum's suppliers, investor positioning tells a more cautious story. The decline in hedge fund ownership and short interest approaching 9% suggest that some investors remain skeptical of the premium valuation. Whether Lumentum can build capacity quickly enough will determine if its premium valuation can hold.

news.Title: Arm vs. Lumentum: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
As artificial intelligence (AI) pushes computing power and data transmission to new limits, investors are weighing different paths to growth. Is Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) or Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) the better choice today?

Arm creates the foundational blueprints for the world's most energy-efficient processors. Lumentum provides the optical components that allow data centers to communicate at lightning speeds. Both companies are central to the infrastructure of modern computing, but they operate with vastly different business models and financial profiles.

The case for Arm

Arm designs and licenses central processing units (CPUs) and other systems used in everything from smartphones to high-performance data centers. Rather than manufacturing chips, the company earns revenue through licensing fees and royalties on every chip sold. This model enables high scalability and profit margins in the semiconductor industry .

In fiscal 2026 (ending in March), Arm's revenue reached $4.9 billion. This represents growth of nearly 23% compared to the prior year. Net income was roughly $698 million, though the net margin decreased slightly from roughly 16% in the previous year to about 14%.

As of its June 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.1x, indicating the company has very little debt relative to its net equity. The current ratio is roughly 5.3x, suggesting a strong ability to meet short-term financial obligations.

Trailing-12-month (TTM) free cash flow was $1.5 billion through the June quarter, but note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 69% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Lumentum

Lumentum manufactures optical and photonic products essential to cloud data centers and telecommunications networks. In its latest fiscal year ended June 27, 2026, Lumentum revealed that Customer A accounted for approximately 26.6% of revenue while Customer B accounted for roughly 15%. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as the loss of either client would be significant.

For fiscal 2026, the company reported revenue of $3 billion, which was an increase of about 83% over the prior year. Despite this massive top-line growth, the company reported a net loss of approximately $6.9 billion, although its operating profit (earnings before interest and taxes) was $525 million. The $6.9 billion net loss was due to a $7.7 billion non-recurring loss on debt extinguishment.

Story Continues

According to its June 2026 balance sheet, the company has a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.4x. The current ratio is nearly 1.7x, indicating about $1.70 in short-term assets for every $1.00 of short-term debt.

TTM free cash flow for the period was roughly $300 million. However, stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 22.7% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

Arm faces intense competition from established rivals and open-source alternatives. If major tech companies decide to design their own architectures rather than paying licensing fees, the company could see its market share erode. Additionally, the business relies on continued growth in the mobile and data center markets, and any slowdown in hardware upgrades would impact its royalty income.

Lumentum is highly dependent on a small number of customers for a significant portion of its sales, and many relationships lack long-term volume commitments. The company is also subject to complex trade policies and export controls, specifically regarding operations in China. Competition from global firms such as IPG Photonics and Viavi Solutions exerts constant pressure on pricing and operating margins.

Valuation comparison

Lumentum appears to be the more value-oriented choice as it trades at a significant discount to its peer across both sales and future earnings estimates.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

Arm is a great business that generates high margins from royalties and licensing fees. It would be a solid chip stock to own, but Lumentum offers better value right now.

Analysts expect Arm to grow earnings at a 25% annualized rate in the coming years. However, Lumentum is expected to deliver 132% annualized growth, as the business scales and expands margins. Relative to their forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios, Arm looks expensive, trading at a forward P/E-to-growth (PEG) ratio of 4.3x, while Lumentum trades at an attractive 0.29x.

Lumentum is benefiting from data centers shifting to optical connectivity for AI workloads. Revenue surged 109% year over year in the recent quarter, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of growth and signaling strong momentum that may not be fully reflected in the stock's valuation right now.

Arm is benefiting from the growing demand for CPUs, and its expertise in designing power-efficient chips could help it gain market share in the data center market.

Both companies are meeting demand at crucial chokepoints for AI, and they both face comparable risks. But it's difficult for me to pass up the huge discrepancy between each stock's PEG ratios. I would buy Lumentum since it's growing much faster than Arm and commands a much lower premium for future earnings growth.

news.Title: Meta's AI vision doesn't come cheap, and its earnings could prove it
news.Content:
Meta ( META ) has enjoyed a wave of favorable headlines with its new products over the past month, but bullish Wall Street may be reminded of one thing when the company reports earnings on Wednesday.

Bringing CEO Mark Zuckerberg's AI vision to life doesn't come cheap.

"Our overall take is that Meta will qualitatively guide to capex and total expense levels that are above the Street, and hence we believe it is probable that Meta's Street [earnings] estimates for 2027 come down," Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney warned. "Our uneducated guess is that management will guide for total expense growth in 2027 at a somewhat slower percentage growth rate than in 2026," or about 40% year over year, and capital expenditures dollar growth "similar to 2026," or around $70 billon.

How the Street would interpret an even more aggressive spending tone by Meta is murky. For one, the stock has rallied a solid 6% in the past month amid a barrage of new product drops .

Meta officially launched its newest frontier AI systems, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full , in the past week. The models are engineered specifically for multistep reasoning, coding, and autonomous personal agent workflows.

They are the first new models from Meta's new Superintelligence Labs. So far, they are receiving high praise for their speeds compared to the likes of OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) GPT-6 and Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) Claude Opus 5.5, spurring optimism about Meta's ability to compete for big enterprise business in the AI boom.

Meanwhile, the Muse AI agent — released in September — appears to be off to a strong adoption start .

The argument could be made that the Street is overlooking Meta's cost of building out AI, given that the stock has rallied steadily. On the other hand, the Street could embrace higher spending to support the growth of praised products.

All in, it's a confusing setup on the stock heading into the earnings report.

"We continue to view Meta as a core name to own as the AI Revolution moves from models to agents, because a frontier model paired with 3.6 billion daily users is a combination few competitors can match," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said.

news.Title: Apple extends iPhone Duo delivery, disappointing eager customers
news.Content:
Apple's first foldable iPhone didn't last long on the shelf. Preorders for the $1,999 iPhone Duo sold out within minutes after opening on Oct. 16, and delivery dates jumped from Oct. 23 to late January. It's also Apple's first book-style foldable, after years of watching Samsung and Google build the market.

Wall Street noticed right away. "Apple opened iPhone Duo pre-orders this morning, and the early read looks robust in our view," Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives wrote in a research note, adding that demand is running well ahead of supply, as reported by CBS News . Folded up, the Duo is roughly the size of a passport.

Also read: Apple just made a surprising move with a popular product

The $1,999 Duo sold out fast, and the wait is long

The rush started before the store even opened. Apple's "Get Ready" process, which lets buyers save their choices ahead of time, closed late on Oct. 15, and every model sold out within about 30 minutes of preorders, after store opening at 8 a.m. ET the next morning, according to Forbes . The phone hadn't even been reviewed yet, and it hits stores on Oct. 23.

Some buyers barely had time to blink. "It's been 3 minutes, and it's sold out at every store around the NYC/CT area," Creativestrat analyst Max Weinbach posted on X. Apple didn't immediately say how many preorders it had taken.

Tight supply was always part of the story. Morgan Stanley analyst Erik Woodring warned in September that supply might fall short of early demand, despite the fact that ("writing that") Apple appeared more focused on securing enough components than finding enough buyers. He expected Apple to have built 7 million to 8 million foldable iPhones in the second half of 2026.

Woodring was impressed by Apple's Sept. 9 event, hosted by CEO John Ternus, calling it the company's most consequential launch since the iPhone X. Morgan Stanley also estimates that with a significant share of Apple customers still running older devices, the iPhone upgrade opportunity remains large.

What the $1,999 actually buys

The Duo is Apple's most ambitious iPhone yet. It has a 5.4-inch front display and a 7.6-inch foldable inner screen with a nano-texture finish that cuts glare and makes the center crease all but invisible. Users can also run two apps side by side.

The fold opens up some new tricks. The phone can sit like a small laptop, with content on the top half and controls on the bottom, or stand like a tent for movies or a bedside clock, as reported by Yahoo Finance . It's equipped with wide and ultrawide rear cameras, but no telephoto lens. Up front, Apple's Center Stage camera helps keep users in view as they move, and a FaceTime camera sits hidden beneath the main folding screen.

Story Continues

Storage ranges from 256GB to 2TB. Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan called the Duo the standout of Apple's event and pointed to features like dual capture in FaceTime, and apps built for the larger display, as reasons it could reach a wider audience, TheStreet reported . Mohan kept his Buy rating on the stock.

Apple shows up late, as it often does

Apple is walking into a market Samsung has worked on for years. Samsung entered foldables in 2019, and its Galaxy Z Fold8 starts at $1,899, about $100 less than Apple's new Duo. The two companies are competing for the consumer while also remaining tied through the hardware supply chain. Apple's huge base of iPhone users, though, could change the economics of the whole category.

Foldables are still a small slice of the phone market. Worldwide foldable shipments were forecast to reach 20.6 million units in 2025, and foldables should make up more than 10% of total smartphone market value by 2029, as reported by IDC . IDC also expects Apple's foldable to take more than 22% of unit share in its first year.

More Apple:

Apple's biggest AI advantage may face new privacy challenge

Apple secret new device is a challenge to Amazon

Bank of America warns Apple investors because of Meta's Muse

The category just hit a major milestone, too. Global foldable shipments should pass 100 million cumulative units by the end of 2026, and Apple could grab about a quarter of the market in its first year, good for second place behind Samsung. Samsung is forecast to keep the lead with 38% of the market.

Some fans are already sold. "I think the 18 is incremental, but the Duo is revolutionary," CNBC's Jim Cramer said after visiting Apple's Manhattan store, adding that he plans to buy one as a second phone, TheStreet reported . Still, one buyer's enthusiasm isn't proof of broad demand.

What investors should watch next

The big question is how many Duos Apple can actually ship. Ives expects demand to stay strong into 2027 and projects Apple will sell about 10 million Duos over the next few quarters and up to 25 million altogether in 2027.

The Duo could also cushion a softer quarter. JPMorgan expects the foldable and higher prices to offset a temporary December-quarter shortfall, while Citi called it Apple's "biggest new hardware category since the Apple Watch and AirPods," as reported by TheStreet . Apple reports fiscal fourth-quarter results on Nov. 2.

The numbers at stake are big. Morgan Stanley estimated the foldable could bring in almost $14 billion in sales in the December quarter alone. If Apple can't build enough of them, though, some of that demand could slip into next year.

news.Title: Can The Trade Desk's Cash Reserves Strengthen Its Competitive Edge?
news.Content:
The Trade Desk 's TTD strong liquidity position provides financial flexibility as it invests in artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance the advertising platform and expand strategic partnerships. As the digital advertising market becomes increasingly competitive, the company's financial resources could help support innovation and strengthen its position in the programmatic advertising industry.

As of June 30, 2026, The Trade Desk had approximately $1.49 billion in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, comprising $1.12 billion in cash and equivalents and $362.4 million in short-term investments. The company also had approximately $745 million available as of June 30 under its revolving credit facility, providing additional financial flexibility.

The Trade Desk generated $154 million in operating cash flow and $136 million in free cash flow during the second quarter. For the first six months of 2026, operating cash flow reached $545.4 million, compared with $456.4 million in the prior-year period.

The company's financial resources support continued investments in its AI-powered Kokai platform, Audience Unlimited and advanced measurement capabilities. In August, TTD unveiled Kokai Zuma, the latest release of its Kokai platform. Zuma brings new agentic AI capabilities and a simpler measurement framework to improve navigation on the Kokai platform for buyers and focus more closely on business outcomes.

In September, the company expanded its healthcare advertising capabilities through enhanced integrations with Veeva Crossix and IQVIA Digital. This move gives pharmaceutical advertisers access to more granular campaign measurement and enables them to use healthcare-specific insights directly in media optimization and decision-making.

Management is also prioritizing platform efficiency through the transition of critical workloads to owned data centers from third-party cloud providers.

The Trade Desk is also balancing growth investments with shareholder returns. The company used $78 million of cash for share repurchases in the quarter, leaving $269 million worth of stock authorized for future buybacks as of June 30, 2026.

Nevertheless, an abrupt slowdown in revenue growth is concerning. On the last earnings call, The Trade Desk highlighted ongoing pressure in key verticals such as Food & Drink and Home & Garden as CPG brands face geopolitical tensions, inflation and consumer softness. While automotive remains strong, it is also impacted by tariffs. CPG and autos generate about 25% of Trade Desk's business, increasing exposure to cautious enterprise budgets.

Story Continues

These pressures were visible in the second quarter of 2026, when revenues rose only 3% year over year to $715.1 million. Management's third-quarter guidance calls for revenues of at least $650 million and assumes no meaningful improvement in the macro backdrop.

Rising infrastructure costs and competitive pricing pressures could constrain profitability and future cash generation. Management's emphasis on disciplined capital allocation will therefore be crucial amid intense competition.

Competitive Landscape

Walled gardens like Meta Platforms, Alphabet GOOGL and Amazon AMZN offer fierce competition in this space as they control their inventory and first-party user data, allowing for highly targeted ad campaigns.

While CTV remains a strong revenue driver, this market is also increasingly becoming competitive as smaller players like Magnite MGNI and PubMatic intensify their efforts.

Alphabet dominates the digital ad space with its online ad platform. The main sources of its ad revenues are Google Search, YouTube ads and Google Network. Alphabet ended the second quarter of 2026 with $242.47 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, while long-term debt stood at $98.17 billion.

Amazon's DSP platform enables advertisers to plan, activate and measure full-funnel investments. The company is also strengthening its position in CTV and premium video advertising.

Earlier, Amazon announced a partnership with OpenAI to support advertising in ChatGPT, expanding its reach into conversational AI. The new partnership will allow advertisers to expand their Amazon Ads campaigns to ChatGPT, with select advertisers in the U.S. testing the integration.

The company is strengthening its advertising capabilities through AI-powered tools such as Ads Agent, which reduces campaign setup and targeting time. As of June 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were $78.2 billion, while the long-term debt totaled $128.9 billion.

Magnite is an independent sell-side advertising company. Its core growth engine, CTV business, continues to deliver strong performance. The company is also expanding its agentic AI capabilities. Earlier in the year, MGNI unveiled Magnite Orchestration, which gained additional omnichannel capabilities and third-party integrations in September. As of June 30, 2026, Magnite had a cash balance of $333 million.

news.Title: US futures rebound as AI earnings test looms; France pressures Europe
news.Content:
By Danilo Masoni

MILAN, Oct 19 (Reuters) - Wall Street futures rose on Monday as oil prices fell and tech shares rebounded ahead of a big week for AI earnings, though concerns about France's fiscal outlook weighed on European assets.

Nasdaq futures climbed 1%, recovering some ‌ground after a bruising week that saw the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index post its longest losing streak since 2008.

S&P 500 futures rose 0.4%, while ‌lower oil prices and safe-haven demand helped support Treasuries after a recent bond selloff unsettled technology stocks and intensified scrutiny of the AI sector's massive funding needs.

With results due from Meta on ​Wednesday, alongside those from Tesla and chipmakers Lam Research and Texas Instruments, markets will be watching for signs that massive AI spending ultimately pays off.

"Investors will want to hear more than another ambitious spending plan: they will want evidence that AI is helping generate enough revenue and profit to justify the bill," said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote.

Meta is one of five AI hyperscalers expected to increase combined capital expenditure to about $1.2 trillion next year, according to Goldman Sachs.

In the second ‌quarter, the Facebook owner reported a sharp decline in ⁠free cash flow as spending accelerated, underscoring the financial strain of the costly AI infrastructure buildout.

Results from SpaceX are also due on Tuesday. Overall, US earnings are still expected to rise about 30%, largely driven by the technology sector.

Benchmark 10-year Treasury ⁠yields fell 2.3 basis points to 5.075%, extending a rally after posting their biggest weekly decline in more than eight months.

FRENCH STRESS WEIGHS ON EUROPE

In Europe, the picture was markedly different. While the region's technology stocks tracked Nasdaq futures higher, concerns over France's fiscal outlook weighed on equities, the euro and government bonds.

Paris blue chips fell 1.5%, ​moving ​back towards the six-month low touched earlier this month, while the pan-European STOXX 600 ​slipped 1%. Banking stocks, seen as particularly vulnerable to sovereign ‌stress, dropped 2.1%.

Widespread weekend unrest in the euro zone's second-largest economy underscored the challenge facing the French government as it seeks to reduce its large budget deficit ahead of next year's presidential elections.

That pushed French bond yields higher and widened their spread over safer German equivalents. France's 10-year bond yield rose 9 bps to 4.875%, while Germany's benchmark yields rose 1.8 bps at 3.428%.

Story Continues

"There is clearly political risk and that is going to mean near-term volatility," said Kiran Ganesh, a multi-asset strategist at UBS Global Wealth Management.

He also noted, however, that roughly 80% of revenues by French stocks come from overseas, limiting the direct impact ‌of political developments on corporate fundamentals.

The euro fell 0.16% to $1.1223, not too far from last ​week's 16-month low of $1.1113, while the dollar index rose roughly 0.1% to 101.9.

OIL RETREATS FROM ​FIVE-MONTH HIGHS

A fall in oil prices following US President Donald Trump's ​decision to waive some sanctions on Russia provided support for broader markets, though investors stayed focused on the potential for conflicts ‌in the Middle East and Ukraine to alter the global ​supply-demand balance.

Brent crude futures fell 1.3%, to $108.4 ​after settling at a five-month high on Friday, while US crude lost 0.3% to $101.15 a barrel.

Earlier in Asia, trading was mixed. Japan's Nikkei fell 0.6%, while MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan edged up 0.1%.

news.Title: Here is What to Know Beyond Why Intel Corporation (INTC) is a Trending Stock
news.Content:
Intel (INTC) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Over the past month, shares of this world's largest chipmaker have returned -17.3%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +1.5% change. During this period, the Zacks Semiconductor - General industry, which Intel falls in, has lost 0.7%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Intel is expected to post earnings of $0.39 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +69.6%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +0.6%.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $1.5 points to a change of +257.1% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed +0.2%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $1.97 indicates a change of +31.4% from what Intel is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +0.5%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Intel.

Story Continues

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS

Projected Revenue Growth

While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. After all, it's nearly impossible for a company to increase its earnings for an extended period without increasing its revenues. So, it's important to know a company's potential revenue growth.

In the case of Intel, the consensus sales estimate of $16.43 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +20.3%. The $62.49 billion and $71.58 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +18.2% and +14.5%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Intel reported revenues of $16.13 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +25.4%. EPS of $0.42 for the same period compares with -$0.1 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $14.41 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +11.89%. The EPS surprise was +100%.

The company beat consensus EPS estimates in each of the trailing four quarters. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.

Valuation

No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

As part of the Zacks Style Scores system, the Zacks Value Style Score (which evaluates both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics) organizes stocks into five groups ranging from A to F (A is better than B; B is better than C; and so on), making it helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Intel is graded F on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Conclusion

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Intel. However, its Zacks Rank #2 does suggest that it may outperform the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: Meta, Tesla, Nvidia, Micron and Alphabet  are part of Zacks Earnings Preview
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 19, 2026 – Zacks.com releases the list of companies likely to issue earnings surprises. This week's list includes Meta META, Tesla TSLA, Nvidia NVDA, Micron MU and Alphabet GOOGL.

Q3 Earnings Season Preview: Revenue Beats Lag, Multi-Sector Momentum Holds

We get into the heart of the Q3 earnings season this week, with more than 250 companies reporting results, including 73 S&P 500 members. By the end of this week, we will have seen Q3 results from 118 S&P 500 members, or almost a quarter of the index's total membership.

We are off to a bit of a mixed start in the Q3 reporting cycle, with the growth pace and the revenue-beat percentage tracking modestly lower relative to the recent past. That said, the sample of results from the 9% of S&P 500 members that have reported is heavily weighted toward the Finance sector, and these initial mixed trends may shift as we head into the heart of the earnings season in the days ahead.

This week's line-up of earnings releases is comprised of a fairly representative cohort of bellwether operators from a broad mix of sectors and industries, including two of the Mag 7 players, Meta Platforms and Tesla, and several other Tech players like Netflix, Texas Instruments, IBM, Spotify, and others. We will get results from air carriers (United, American, Southwest), railroad operators (CSX, Union Pacific), credit card issuers (American Express, Capital One, Synchrony), and many other blue chips like Procter & Gamble, GM, AT&T, Halliburton, and others.

We will have a definitive sense of how good or otherwise the Q3 earnings season has been by the end of this week.

Looking at overall expectations for the quarter, combining the actual results from the 45 S&P 500 members that have reported already with estimates for the still-to-come companies, Q3 earnings are currently expected to increase by +24.6% from the same period last year on +11.7% higher revenues, the 8th straight quarter of double-digit earnings growth for the index.

The Tech sector remains a major growth contributor, but momentum is broad-based, with 14 of the 16 Zacks sectors on track for positive earnings growth in Q3. Importantly, the revisions trend remains positive and broad-based, highlighting a steadily improving outlook.

As noted earlier, the revisions trend has been positive, sustaining the favorable trend in place for almost a year. Estimates for Q3 increased after the quarter got underway, and we are seeing a similar trend at play for 2026 Q4 estimates.

Story Continues

This positive revisions behavior is not a new development; it extends a tailwind that has been building for nearly a year. The positive revisions were at first concentrated in Technology and, more recently, Energy, following Middle East supply disruptions. However, for 2026 Q4 and also what we saw for Q3, the constructive estimate revisions have broadened significantly, rising across 7 of the 16 Zacks sectors—including Aerospace, Construction, Industrials, Finance, and Transportation alongside Tech and Energy.

On the negative side, Q4 estimates remain under pressure for these 8 sectors – Conglomerates, Autos, Basic Materials, Consumer Staples, Consumer Discretionary, Medical, Business Services, and Retail. It is important to note that estimates for full-year 2027 have also been trending higher.

Sector Focus: Broad-Based Strength

Q3 earnings are expected to be above the year-earlier level for 14 of the 16 Zacks sectors, with 5 sectors expected to enjoy double-digit growth. The Conglomerates and Consumer Staples sectors are the only ones expected to have lower earnings in Q3 relative to the same period last year.

The 5 sectors expected to enjoy double-digit earnings growth in Q3 are Aerospace (up +160.5%), Energy (+122.2%), Tech (+43.7%), Basic Materials (+29.5%), Transportation (+9.6%), and Industrial Products (+13.5%).

Q3 earnings growth for the S&P 500 index drops to +20.1% from +24.6% once the Energy sector's contribution is excluded from the index. Excluding the Tech sector, Q3 earnings growth for the rest of the index drops to +14.4%.

For the Finance sector, which has dominated the reporting docket thus far, Q3 earnings are expected to be up +7.3% from the same period last year on +6.3% higher revenues.

With Meta and Tesla on deck to report results this week, it is useful to take a look at expectations for the Mag 7 group as a whole. The expectation is that Q3 earnings for the Mag 7 will increase by +20.9% on +22.8% higher revenues.

Excluding the Mag 7 group's contribution, Q3 earnings for the rest of the index would actually modestly improve to +25.8% (from +24.6%).

The Q3 earnings and revenue growth rate drops to +21.1% from +43.7% once the substantial contributions from Nvidia , Micron and Alphabet are excluded, as the chart below shows.

Q3 Earnings Season Scorecard

Through Friday, October 16th, we have seen Q3 results from 45 S&P 500 members, or 9% of the index's total membership. Total earnings for these companies are up +46.3% from the same period last year on +13.9% higher revenues, with 82.2% beating EPS estimates and 62.2% beating revenue estimates.

The very strong earnings and revenue growth pace for this group of 45 S&P 500 members is mostly due to Micron, whose Q3 earnings increased +1075.7% from the year-earlier level. Excluding Micron, Q3 earnings for the remaining 44 index members that have reported would be up +10.4%.

For the Finance sector, we now have Q3 results from 44.3% of the sector's market capitalization in the S&P 500 index. Total earnings for these Finance sector companies are up +10.6% from the same period last year on +8.6% higher revenues, with 80% beating EPS estimates and 50% beating revenue estimates.

Not only are the growth rates tracking below other recent periods, but Finance sector companies also seem to be struggling to beat consensus EPS and revenue estimates.

The Earnings Big Picture

As we noted earlier, estimates for full-year 2027 are experiencing the same positive and broad-based revisions trend that we noted earlier in the context of 2026 Q4.

Datadog rose 3.6% in premarket trading after Bernstein SocGen Group upgraded the cloud monitoring and AI observability company to Outperform from Market Perform and raised its price target to $350 from $237, an increase of nearly 48%.

The upgrade marked a shift in the broker's view after it downgraded the stock last quarter following the downsizing of a roughly $100 million annual recurring revenue contract with its largest "Born in AI" customer, believed to be OpenAI, alongside signs of weakness among traditional customers, which account for around 85% of revenue.

The analyst had also expected growth among "Born in AI" customers to slow to around 50% to 60% in 2027, from 80% to 90% this year. The latest upgrade suggests a more positive assessment of the company's growth prospects despite those earlier concerns.

Intel gained nearly 4% in premarket trading after JPMorgan upgraded the chipmaker to Neutral from Underweight late Friday, citing a more balanced risk-reward profile as the stock approached the firm's $85 price target following a roughly 36% decline from its June peak.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Analyst Harlan Sur said Intel's turnaround would take years but noted that management had made a solid start and that his confidence in the recovery was increasing. He also pointed to continued support from AI-related demand as a potential tailwind for the business.

Red Cat Holdings climbed 6.6% after announcing a voluntary public all-cash tender offer to acquire all outstanding shares of Austrian engine manufacturer Steyr Motors AG for €39 per share through its wholly owned Vienna-based subsidiary, SMOT Acquisition GmbH.

The offer represents a 28.9% premium to Steyr Motors' October 16 closing price and a 27.3% premium to its 30-day volume-weighted average price. The transaction values the deal at approximately €204.8 million, or around $230 million.

Story Continues

The acquisition would support Red Cat's Blue Ops uncrewed surface vessel division by adding Steyr Motors' expertise in high-performance marine propulsion systems used in mission-critical military and civilian applications.

Nebius Group rose 3.6% in premarket trading as the AI infrastructure company attempted to recover from a sharp selloff that had erased roughly 21% of its market value over the previous week. The stock had closed at $165.47 on October 16 after falling nearly 12% in that session amid broader weakness in AI infrastructure shares.

Sentiment improved after Truist analysts reiterated Buy ratings on both Nebius and CoreWeave, assigning Nebius a $355 price target. The endorsement offered support to the stock as investors reassessed valuations and financing risks across the AI infrastructure sector.

Silgan Holdings advanced 5.5% after announcing plans to acquire Trivium Packaging in a $3.4 billion transaction alongside American Industrial Partners, creating a combined metal packaging business.

The deal will bring together Silgan's Metal Containers segment and its Food and Beverage Flat Cap Closures businesses with Trivium to form Silgan Metal Containers and Closures. The all-cash transaction values Trivium at an enterprise value of approximately $3.4 billion, equivalent to 7.1 times its last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, or 4.8 times after accounting for expected synergies of $225 million.

news.Content: 台股今（19）日開低走低，盤中受國際市場恐慌情緒影響，一度狂拉警報重挫941.26點至46,170.00點，終場收在46,822.08點，下跌289.18點，跌幅0.61%，總成交額達8,251億元。儘管大盤盤中面臨驚心動魄的沉重賣壓，卻在季線附近展現強勁防守韌性，硬生生拉出逾600點的長下影線。對此， 摩爾證券投顧分析師江國中 指出，短線劇烈暴跌僅是籌碼洗盤與情緒宣洩，非AI基本面轉壞，隨著指標落入超賣區， 本週三期貨結算過後，台股極可能迎來高達2,500點以上的波段強彈行情！ 【恐慌拋售潮席捲盤面 歷史數據解密轉折契機】 江國中解釋，盤中台股大跌941點後拉出652點的長下影線，顯示季線防守力道非常強勁。隨著週三期貨結算完成壓低洗盤與籌碼換手，極可能成為大盤正式展開絕地大反攻的時間轉折點，有很大的機率會迎接2,500 點以上的強彈與暴利。 面對費城半導體指數連跌引發的全球股市震盪，許多散戶在最恐慌時被迫砍在最低點。但江國中翻開台股歷史統計數據分析，外資史上前十大單日賣超紀錄發生後，大盤平均僅需2.4天就能見到波段低點，且通常只需8.6天就能完全吃掉當天的黑K跌幅。 全球最大避險基金橋水基金（Bridgewater Associates）的創辦人瑞·達利歐（Ray Dalio）曾提醒，高檔賣出後最難的是何時重新買回，若錯過暴跌過後的單日大漲，往往也錯過了最猛烈的波段行情。「下跌時如果沒有小麥，噴出時你也不會有小麥」，江國中強調，今日盤中的大甩尾，正暗示著市場最沉痛的籌碼洗盤已接近尾聲。 【PCB上游迎急單喊漲 聰明資金打臉AI泡沫論】 力挺這波多頭反攻氣勢的核心，正是被譽為AI工業基石的PCB產業。近期包含玻纖布、銅箔與銅箔基板（CCL）等PCB上游材料紛紛調漲價格，市場聰明資金不僅沒有退縮，反而欣然買單推升股價，證明下游急需產能、訂單應接不暇，直接打臉市場對AI泡沫的疑慮。 被譽為「PCB之母」的大量（3167）持續展現長線成長力道；而高階鑽針廠尖點（8021）更獲得欣興（3037）、臻鼎-KY（4958）等載板與PCB巨頭親自注資擴產，7至9月營收連創歷史新高，凸顯產業基本面的扎實與強勁需求。

news.Title: Why Intel stock just got a big upgrade
news.Content:
After a sweeping tech stock sell-off last week, Wall Street is on the hunt for bargains.

And JPMorgan ( JPM ) may have found one in chip giant Intel ( INTC ), with the stock off about 36% from the June highs. Analyst Harlan Sur upgraded his rating on Intel to Neutral from Underweight on Monday.

Intel stock rose 4% in premarket trading.

Here are several of Sur's thoughts that stood out:

CEO is driving fundamental change: "More importantly, since Lip Bu Tan's appointment to CEO, we believe the team's execution and competitiveness in their core client/datacenter compute market has improved, the team's execution on next-gen manufacturing has significantly improved (yields, manufacturability, foundry process/design rule compatibility, advanced packaging) and the team has several initiatives (ASICs) which exploit INTC's strong IP portfolio, SOC design capabilities, and leading edge internal manufacturing capabilities."

Estimates could be poised for lift-off: "Despite near-term concerns on AI infrastructure spending sustainability, we believe increasing agentic AI workloads (CPU intensive) and a very tight supply chain for leading edge silicon should drive continued positive EPS revisions in the upcoming earnings season and through CY27 (our CY28 EPS estimates are ~15% above consensus)."

news.Title: Can Ad-Supported Streaming Momentum Boost Netflix's Q3 Results?
news.Content:
Netflix NFLX is slated to report third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 20.

Management has guided revenues of $12.86 billion, implying roughly 12% year-over-year growth (11% on a foreign-exchange-neutral basis), with adjusted earnings per share (EPS) projected at 82 cents and net income at $3.45 billion. The key question is whether ad momentum has offset slower engagement growth and rising costs.

Netflix, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Netflix, Inc. price-eps-surprise | Netflix, Inc. Quote

Click here to know how the company's overall third-quarter performance is expected to be.

Advertising Likely Acted as a Key Growth Lever

Advertising is expected to have been the standout driver. Netflix targets roughly $3 billion in 2026 ad revenues, about double the 2025 level. In August, the company closed its 2026 U.S. Upfront with commitments nearly doubling year over year, while game sponsorships for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup sold out. Programmatic access, extended to Pause Ads and live inventory this summer through Alphabet 's GOOGL Google Display & Video 360, Amazon AMZN, Yahoo and The Trade Desk, along with the Media Rating Council's first accreditation of the Netflix Ads Suite, is likely to have improved monetization. In September, Netflix hosted its first UK Upfront, unveiling income and household-composition targeting. However, the ad-tier expansion into nine EMEA countries begins only in March 2027, limiting near-term contribution, and ad revenues remain a small portion of total revenue.

Live programming is expected to have supported engagement and ad inventory. Netflix streamed MLB's Home Run Derby on July 13 and the Field of Dreams game on Aug. 13, followed by the NFL's Week 1 Rams-49ers matchup in Melbourne on Sept. 10. Yet live content accounts for about 5% of 2026 content spend but only about 1% of view hours, likely pressuring returns.

The content slate, including Outer Banks ' final season, The Hawk, Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story, The Gentleme n Season 2, 72 Hours and The Whisper Man , is expected to have aided retention. Pricing changes in the United States, Mexico and Spain are expected to have contributed, with UCAN benefiting from a full quarter of the U.S. price increase. Still, first-half view hours grew only 2%, highlighting competition for viewer attention.

On profitability, the third-quarter operating margin is projected at 33.2%, up from 28.2% in the year-ago quarter, which included a Brazilian tax expense. Content amortization is expected to grow approximately 10% in 2026. Capital expenditures remained modest at $414.8 million in the first half, supporting the full-year free cash flow outlook of roughly $12.5 billion. The full-year revenue outlook of $51-$51.4 billion and 31.5% operating margin suggest stable fundamentals, although foreign-exchange volatility and content timing remain risks.

Story Continues

Investment Perspective

Netflix's third-quarter 2026 outlook reflects solid fundamentals, with revenues guided at $12.86 billion, up roughly 12%, and operating margin projected at 33.2%. Ad revenues are targeted to double to about $3 billion in 2026, supported by nearly doubled U.S. Upfront commitments and expanding programmatic access. However, stiff competition from YouTube, Disney DIS-owned Disney+ and Amazon Prime Video for viewer attention, only 2% first-half view-hour growth and costly live sports rights temper the near-term upside. With ad-tier expansion into nine EMEA markets arriving only in March 2027, investors should hold the stock or wait for a better entry point ahead of third-quarter results. news.Title: Dow Jones, Nasdaq, S&P 500 preview: All eyes on Meta, Tesla, SpaceX earnings
news.Content:
Investing.com -- U.S. stocks fell Friday, closing out a mostly losing week as investors retreated from technology and AI-linked names while oil prices rose.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The S&P 500 dropped 1.09% to 7,659.44, and the Nasdaq Composite tumbled 2.14% to 26,140.03, with both indexes finishing below their 50-day moving averages. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 175.28 points, or 0.34%, to 52,002.41. The Cboe Volatility Index climbed above 22 for the first time in four months.

Semiconductor stocks were again at the center of the pullback, with the SOXX ETF falling 4.14%. Those losses, alongside broader weakness in AI-related shares, pulled the S&P 500 down about 2% for the week. The Nasdaq posted its worst weekly performance since June, down more than 4%, while the Dow managed a 0.7% weekly gain.

Despite the rout, the S&P 500 remains only about 2% below the record high it set earlier this month. Sectors that had lagged during last month's tech rally, including healthcare and consumer staples, posted solid gains over the week.

The recent stumble in the AI trade, which has powered much of the market's rally this year, faces a key test in the coming days as investors turn their attention to a wave of corporate earnings. Meta Platforms, one of the hyperscalers pouring billions into AI data center buildouts, headlines this week's reporting calendar.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Also set to report this week are chipmakers Lam Research and Texas Instruments, along with Elon Musk's SpaceX and Tesla. Netflix, consumer goods maker Procter & Gamble, and engine manufacturer GE Aerospace are also scheduled to report earnings.

Additionally, investors this week will parse a fresh batch of economic data, including housing starts and building permits, weekly jobless claims, and preliminary S&P Global PMI readings alongside the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment survey.

What analysts are saying about U.S. equities

JPMorgan : "If bond yields are stabilizing, that will help equities, through allowing the cycle to look more sustainable, through reducing pressure on AI funding, as well as on consumer finances, and through reducing the drive for P/E compression. Indeed, during the most intense phase of yields spiking, forward P/E for AC World fell by 3 points, for SPX by 3 points and for Europe by 2 points. The multiple compression might not need to continue."

Story Continues

Goldman Sachs : "Equity prices should continue to rise as long as earnings grow. Positive but decelerating growth has historically been associated with positive but moderating S&P 500 returns. Equity returns in these environments have historically been driven by earnings growth rather than by valuation expansion. Within the market, a backdrop of positive but decelerating growth usually supports the outperformance of companies with secular growth over those with cyclical growth as well as stocks with price momentum, positive earnings revisions, and low volatility."

Morgan Stanley : "We favor quality in U.S. equities, but see recent volatility creating opportunity in higher-quality cyclicals given still-resilient growth. Capital Goods stands out, and has improving revision breadth."

Evercore ISI: "Last week's NDX selloff was the beginning of the price discovery process as a "perfect storm" for AI/Tech laid down "lines in the sand" that if crossed would transition the AI bull market into a correction, and if accompanied by a recession, could produce an equity bear market."

news.Title: 〈台幣〉熱錢持續流出 重貶1.07角收32.445元
news.Content:
台北金融市場今(19) 日「股匯雙殺」再現，受到美股震盪及國際避險情緒升溫影響，外資持續大舉撤資，三大法人合計賣超台股899.54億元，加權指數一度重挫941點，台積電 (2330-TW) (TSM-US) 等權值股尾盤急拉，終場下跌289.18點，收在46822.08點。匯市在資金大量淨匯出壓力下，新台幣兌美元匯率開低走低，盤中一度觸及32.572元低點，終場重貶1.07角收在32.445元，兩大外匯市場爆出38.53億美元的大量。

觀察台股法人動態，三大法人今日資金操作分歧明顯。外資及陸資延續偏空態度，單日賣超高達767.43億元，寫下連續9個交易日賣超紀錄；自營商也站在賣方，賣超362.63億元；僅投信法人獨撐大局，逆勢買超230.51億元，展現強烈護盤意願。

今日台股籌碼面持續出現調節，導致大盤開盤即遭重挫，盤中最低下探46170點，考驗季線支撐，所幸尾盤台積電等半導體族群拉回平盤，帶動指數跌幅收斂。

匯市方面，新台幣兌美元開盤價為32.36元，隨後受外資強勁匯出買賣盤衝擊，匯價一路下探，早盤最高僅達32.36元，盤中最低重摔至32.572元。面對外資短時間大幅撤離，中央銀行盤中罕見緊急發布聲明穩固信心，並適時進場拋匯提供美元流動性。終場台北外匯市場新台幣收在32.445元，貶值1.07角；成交金額則擴大至28.31億美元。

元太外匯市場新台幣收盤價則為32.468元，貶值1.2角，成交金額為10.22億美元。兩大匯市合計成交金額衝高至38.53億美元，顯示市場交投極為熱絡且多空對峙激烈。
